body.statement: The map \(\Phi\) extends real analytically to an open neighborhood of every regular \(p\) satisfying the identification assumptions. In the saturated finite-multinomial model on the declared support stratum, \(G_p(s)=J_{\Phi}(p)(e_s-p)\) is the canonical gradient of \(\Phi(p)\), \(\Sigma(p)\) is its information bound, and the empirical-cell plug-in attains this bound at every relative-interior law on that stratum.
body.justification: Analyticity makes the influence function explicit and turns a constructive identification formula into a regular finite-multinomial estimator.
body.gap: Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin differentiate simultaneous-diagonalization estimators for nonexchangeable latent models, while Ahn and Kasahara use interior likelihood asymptotics; neither gives the canonical gradient of this row-sum and pseudoinverse map on an absorbing support stratum.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a closed-form delta-method variance that includes estimated type masses and avoids repeated nonconvex likelihood optimization.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q_d(p)=\sum_{s:D(s)=d}p_s\).  By \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(q_d(p)>0\), and every cohort-conditional entry used in \(A_{xy}^d\) and \(m_x^d\) is a linear function of \(p\) divided by \(q_d(p)\).  The proof of \(\texttt{thm:face-recovery}\) shows at every compatible regular \(p\) that all four slice determinants, \(\det(B_a^d)\), \(\det(W^d)\), \(\det(B_b^d)\), every row-sum normalizer used in division, every recovered type mass, and every \(\det\{C_y^d(C_y^d)^\top\}\) are nonzero, while the discriminant \((g^d)^2\) is strictly positive.

Let \(\mathcal U_p\) be the set in the affine hyperplane \(\{z:\mathbf1^\top z=1\}\) on which the same finitely many denominators remain nonzero and both discriminants remain positive.  These are strict conditions on continuous functions, so \(\mathcal U_p\) is a relative open neighborhood of \(p\).  Cohort conditioning and matrix inversion are rational maps there.  The positive square-root function is real analytic on \((0,\infty)\), and
\[
 C^\dagger=C^\top(CC^\top)^{-1}                              \tag{16}
\]
is analytic whenever \(CC^\top\) is nonsingular.  The construction in \(\texttt{def:recovery-map}\) is a finite composition of these rational maps, the positive square root, sums, and products.  Hence \(\Phi\) is real analytic on \(\mathcal U_p\).  Notice that this is an off-model analytic extension: coordinates of \(z\in\mathcal U_p\) need not all be nonnegative.

For completeness, the Jacobian is actionable rather than merely existential.  For a tangent direction \(h\) with \(\mathbf1^\top h=0\), put a dot over every recovered quantity to denote its directional derivative.  First,
\[
 \dot q_d=\sum_{s:D(s)=d}h_s,
 \qquad
 \frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\frac{p_s+\varepsilon h_s}{q_d(p+\varepsilon h)}\bigg|_{\varepsilon=0}
 =\frac{h_s}{q_d}-\frac{p_s\dot q_d}{q_d^2}.                 \tag{17}
\]
All slice derivatives follow by the indicated marginal sums.  The remaining recursion is
\[
 \dot M^{-1}=-M^{-1}\dot M M^{-1},\qquad
 \dot g=\frac{2\operatorname{tr}(K)\operatorname{tr}(\dot K)-4\dot{\det K}}{2g},                 \tag{18}
\]
where, for a \(2\times2\) matrix,
\[
 \dot{\det K}=K_{22}\dot K_{11}+K_{11}\dot K_{22}-K_{21}\dot K_{12}-K_{12}\dot K_{21}.         \tag{19}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \dot\rho_{1,2}=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\dot K)\mathbin{\pm}\dot g}{2},\quad
 \dot P_1=\frac{\dot K-\dot\rho_2I_2}{g}-\frac{\dot g}{g}P_1,
 \quad \dot P_2=-\dot P_1,                                  \tag{20}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot B_a[:,j]&=\dot P_jm_a+P_j\dot m_a,\\
 \dot F_y&=-B_a^{-1}\dot B_aF_y+B_a^{-1}\dot A_{ay},\\
 \dot q_{ay}&=\dot F_y\mathbf1_3,\\
 \dot C_y[j,:]&=\{\dot F_y[j,:]-\dot q_{ay}[j]C_y[j,:]\}/q_{ay}[j].
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{21}
\]
With \(C=C_a\) and \(N=(CC^\top)^{-1}\), differentiation of (16) gives
\[
 \dot C^\dagger=\dot C^\top N-C^\top N(\dot C C^\top+C\dot C^\top)N,                          \tag{22}
\]
followed by
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot W&=\dot A_{ba}C^\dagger+A_{ba}\dot C^\dagger,\\
 \dot c&=W^{-1}(\dot m_b-\dot Wc),\\
 \dot B_b&=\dot W\operatorname{diag}(c)+W\operatorname{diag}(\dot c).
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{23}
\]
For \(y\in\mathcal A\), the second-row normalizers satisfy
\[
 \dot q_{by}=-B_b^{-1}\dot B_bq_{by}+B_b^{-1}\dot A_{by}\mathbf1_3.
\]
Thus the active entries of \(\dot{\widehat Q}_j^d\) are \(\dot q_{ay}[j]\) and \(\dot q_{by}[j]\); its exit entry is minus their sum, and its absorbing-row derivative is zero.  The active rows of \(\dot{\widehat R}_j^d\) are the corresponding rows of \(\dot C_y^d\), and its absorbing-row derivative is zero.  If
\[
 s_j^d=(\mathbf1_2^\top B_a^d[:,j],\mathbf1_2^\top B_b^d[:,j],0),
\]
then
\[
 \dot\pi_j^d=\mathbf1_2^\top\{\dot B_a^d[:,j]+\dot B_b^d[:,j]\},\quad
 \dot p_{1,j}^d=\frac{\dot s_j^d\pi_j^d-s_j^d\dot\pi_j^d}{(\pi_j^d)^2},\quad
 \dot p_{2,j}^d=\dot p_{1,j}^d\widehat Q_j^d+p_{1,j}^d\dot{\widehat Q}_j^d.                    \tag{24}
\]
Finally,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot\tau_j&=\dot p_{2,j}^1(\widehat R_j^1-\widehat R_j^0)
 +p_{2,j}^1(\dot{\widehat R}_j^1-\dot{\widehat R}_j^0),\\
 \dot\tau&=\sum_{j=1}^2\{\dot\pi_j^1\tau_j+\pi_j^1\dot\tau_j\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{25}
\]
Equations (17)--(25) determine \(J_\Phi(p)h\), including the derivative of the recovered type weights.

We next prove the canonical-gradient assertion.  Let \(\mathcal S_0\) denote the finite support stratum containing \(p\), and suppose \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S_0\), which is exactly relative interiority on that stratum.  Every saturated score is a function \(h:\mathcal S_0\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
 E_P h(O)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_0}p_sh(s)=0.                  \tag{26}
\]
Conversely, for any bounded such \(h\), \(p_{\varepsilon,s}=p_s\{1+\varepsilon h(s)\}\) is a probability law for all sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\), and it has score \(h\).  Thus the saturated tangent space is all of \(L_2^0(P)\).  Differentiability of \(\Phi\), (26), and the definition of \(G_p\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\Phi(p_\varepsilon)\right|_{\varepsilon=0}
 &=J_\Phi(p)\sum_s p_se_sh(s)\\
 &=E_P\!\left[J_\Phi(p)(e_O-p)h(O)\right]
 =E_P\{G_p(O)h(O)\},                                         \tag{27}
 \end{aligned}
\]
because \(E_Ph=0\).  Also \(E_PG_p(O)=J_\Phi(p)(p-p)=0\).  If \(H\) is any other centered influence function for the same functional, (27) implies \(E_P\{(H-G_p)h\}=0\) for every \(h\in L_2^0(P)\).  Taking each coordinate of \(H-G_p\) itself as \(h\) proves \(H=G_p\) almost surely.  Hence \(G_p\) is the canonical gradient, and its covariance
\[
 E_P\{G_p(O)G_p(O)^\top\}
 =J_\Phi(p)\{\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^\top\}J_\Phi(p)^\top
 =\Sigma(p)                                                     \tag{28}
\]
is the saturated information bound.  This proves the bound rather than identifying it by definition: for any centered influence function \(H\), the score equations force \(H=G_p\), so the infimum of influence-function covariance matrices in the positive-semidefinite order is exactly (28).

For the empirical-cell plug-in, the multinomial identity gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p-p)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(e_{O_i}-p),
 \qquad \widehat p-p=O_P(n^{-1/2}).                           \tag{29}
\]
Taylor expansion of the analytic map at a fixed interior \(p\) and (29) give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\Phi(\widehat p)-\Phi(p)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nJ_\Phi(p)(e_{O_i}-p)+o_P(1)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nG_p(O_i)+o_P(1).                       \tag{30}
\]
Its influence function is therefore the canonical gradient and its asymptotic covariance is (28), so it attains the saturated finite-multinomial information bound.
